### Observed differences

- In the later window, A02 takes part in far fewer traces: about 21 in 100 versus about 75 in 100 before (mean occurrences per trace 0.23 versus 0.81), and when it does occur it sits earlier and much more variably in the trace (mean relative position about 0.55 versus 0.93). [OCC001, POS001]
- The closing route into A50 changed. Before, about 91 in 100 of A02's outgoing transitions went to A50, and A50 followed A02 within one step in about 99 in 100 observed pairs; in the later window only about 13 in 100 of A02's outgoing transitions go to A50 (the rest spread over many targets), while A49 now sends about 83 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A50 (before about 26 in 100, with about 72 in 100 to A02) and A50 immediately follows A49 in about 84 in 100 cases. [DIR001, LAG001, DIR011, LAG009]
- A block of activities swapped order. Before, A35, A36 and A41 each ran before A26 and A27 in about 97–99 in 100 traces; in the later window A26 and A27 run before A35, A36 and A41 in about 97–98 in 100 traces, with both members of every pair present in all traces in both windows. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015]
- Routing around A27 and A30 changed accordingly. A25 now leads to A27 in about 96 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (before it split across A35, A36 and A41), and A27 immediately follows A25 in about 98 in 100 cases instead of running about four steps later; A26 now spreads its outgoing transitions roughly equally over A35, A36 and A41 (about 35, 32 and 31 in 100) rather than almost always to A30 (about 98 in 100 before); and A35, A36 and A41 now each send about 30–34 in 100 of their outgoing transitions to A30, which previously received almost nothing from them while A27 received about 28–36 in 100 from each. [DIR005, LAG002, DIR006, LAG005, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009]
- Matching the reorder, A35, A36 and A41 now occur later in the trace (mean relative position about 0.40 versus 0.58), while A26 and A27 occur slightly earlier (about 0.60 versus 0.53 and 0.46 versus 0.39). [POS004, POS005, POS006, POS002, POS003]
- A02 now co-occurs with the activities above (A25, A26, A27, A30, A35, A36, A41, A49, A50) in only about 21 in 100 traces versus about 74 in 100 before, with those activities usually appearing without it; this largely restates the participation drop rather than an independent effect. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- Two activities occur more often: A06 is present in about 19 in 100 later traces versus about 6.5 in 100 before, and A10 in about 21.5 versus about 8.5 in 100; A06's outgoing transitions, previously spread evenly over twelve targets on very few observations, now concentrate on A48, A50, A16 and A19. [OCC002, OCC003, DIR002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the flow was restructured in two connected ways. In the segment formed by A25, A26, A27, A35, A36, A41 and A30, the order reversed: A25 is now followed immediately by A27, A26 precedes the A35/A36/A41 cluster instead of following it, and the cluster now leads to A30 (about 30–34 in 100 of outgoing transitions each), whereas previously A27 received those edges and A30 came directly after A26. Separately, A02 was largely taken out of the closing part of the flow — it appears in about a third as many traces, no longer almost always precedes A50, and A49 connects directly to A50 — while A06 and A10 take part in more traces. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, LAG002, LAG005, OCC001, DIR001, DIR011, LAG009, OCC002, OCC003]

The judgement rests on directness and consistency rather than item count alone: 45 qualifying items against well under one (about 0.83) expected if nothing had changed, every item's difference exceeding about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits, and — most importantly — the order reversal is observed directly in trace-relative relations while both activities remain present in 100 in 100 traces of both windows, which rules out a participation change as the cause of the flip; direction, position and lag indicators all point the same way. [REL010, REL015, DIR005, LAG002, POS004]

Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a rewiring of a single process from a shift in the mix of pre-existing variants (for example an old-order and a new-order variant trading dominance); with 200 traces per window and near-deterministic orderings, pure sampling noise is unlikely, but sampling differences in variant frequencies remain a competing explanation. A few lag profiles also rest on very few observations in one window (2–3 supporting observations in the later window for the A25–A36 and A25–A41 pairs, and a single observation in the earlier window for the A26–A36 and A36–A30 pairs), so those details are weakly grounded, though the hypothesis does not depend on them. [LAG003, LAG004, LAG006, LAG008]
